title: Prefetch wavefront and decode handshake synchronizer
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: tail-latency spikes in mixed short/long workloads trace back to prefill bursts that saturate kernel queues and then stall decode steps while KV cache warming proceeds. This PR introduces a lightweight "wavefront" prefetch coordination layer and a decode handshake synchronizer so that prefill kernels emit formal readiness signals before occupying decode resources. Goals: reduce tail latency under continuous-batching workloads, avoid long-lived decode kernel starvation, and maintain KV-cache warmup effectiveness.

Design summary: single-threaded coordination object per GPU pool (PrefetchWavefrontCoordinator) that tracks prefill window boundaries and grants time-sliced decode permits. Prefill operations run as usual but enqueue a compact readiness token instead of immediately grabbing decode semaphore; the Synchronizer batches tokens into decode grant frames to enable controlled overlap across prefills. The handshake is non-blocking for short-prefill flows (small contexts) and backpressures large batched prefill work by deferring decode grants. The coordinator is kernel-agnostic and uses existing kernel launch metadata (sequence length distribution and quantized-window hints) to prioritize grant order.

Key changes (high level): added a coordinator abstraction in runtime/scheduler, wire up a CUDA-side signal channel for kernel-to-runtime readiness (low-overhead flag + epoch id), integrate synchronizer into continuous-batching path, and new metrics/tracing points to expose wavefront latency and grant skew. Also added a micro-benchmark to reproduce mixed short/long workload tails.

Behavioral notes: this intentionally reduces instantaneous decode concurrency during heavy prefill spikes but shifts load to staged decode windows to keep average throughput stable while reducing 99.9p latency. KV cache warmup remains effective because prefetch tokens still carry KV warming hints; the coordinator only controls decode start, not KV population.

Testing and validation: unit tests for coordinator state machine and handshake edge cases, e2e bench under lab harness (mixed 8-token and 2048-token requests) showing 22% reduction in 99.9p tail latency and no regression in median throughput. CI: initial lint/build failed due to header ordering; fixed in second commit.

Migration and rollout: feature gated under runtime flag runtime.experimental.wavefront_prefetch (off by default). Suggested canary rollout to Dedicated customers with synthetic traces before broadly enabling on hosted.

Related: ENG-8421 tracks instrumentation additions; ENG-8489 is the incident ticket prompting this work.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: high-level looks good, but can you explain how this interacts with existing KV soft-evict heuristics? Need to ensure we don't create a steady-state oscillation.

Maya Chen: reply - coordinator only gates decode start; we keep existing soft-evict timers and add a grace window so the eviction heuristics see continuous warming signals. Added tests to validate no oscillation under synthetic traces.
Lena Ortiz: requested change - move metric tag from 'pool' to 'gpu_pool' to align with dashboards
Maya Chen: addressed - updated metrics and dashboards references in commit f7e2b11
Tomás Rivera: approval - saw perf runs and unit tests; please add a short note to the runbook describing the toggle and how to interpret grant skew metrics before rollout.
release_notes: Introduces an experimental wavefront prefetch coordinator and decode handshake synchronizer to reduce 99.9p tail latency under mixed short/long continuous-batching workloads. Feature is gated behind runtime.experimental.wavefront_prefetch.
